title: Regional SLO matrix and fallback rollout criteria for low-latency routes
creator: Oliver Park
description:
PRD: Define a regional SLO matrix (by region and customer tier) and concrete rollout gating for low-latency API routes. Goal: provide precise p50/p95/p99 latency targets and an automated fallback policy for model variants when SLOs are at risk, plus region-specific error budgets and canary thresholds that tie into the Console rollout engine. This ticket scopes the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout gate definitions; engineering will use this to implement routing policies and Console guards.

Background: Hosted customers in EU/NA/APAC experience different latency baselines. We need an explicit mapping from region + tier -> latency SLOs and a deterministic fallback plan (e.g., smaller-quantized variant, local cache-enabled model, or degrade to shorter context) when SLO degradation threatens customer SLAs. Current related work focuses on general SLOs and canary guards but lacks region granularity and explicit fallback decision logic.

Scope (in):
- Define SLO targets (p50/p95/p99) per region (NA, EU, APAC) and per customer tier (Free/Standard/Premium/Dedicated).
- Specify error budget windows and automated gating thresholds for progressive rollouts (canary -> ramp -> global).
- Define fallback hierarchy for model variants and the conditions that trigger each fallback.
- Define Console rollout gate signals (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta, customer-facing errors) and numeric thresholds for each stage.
- Acceptance criteria and monitoring dashboards to validate correctness during rollout.

Scope (out):
- Implementation details of kernel selection or quantization work (handled by infra/runtime tickets).
- Billing/Pricing changes tied to SLO tiers (handled by pricing PM).

Success metrics:
- Rollouts can be automatically halted or rolled back when region-specific p95 exceeds threshold for 10 minutes with >3% customer requests affected.
- No fewer than 95% of Premium traffic remains within defined p95 latency in each region during steady-state.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Overly aggressive fallbacks could reduce quality. Mitigation: Provide QA guardrails and a human approval step for quality-sensitive customers.
- Risk: Metric noise in low-traffic regions. Mitigation: Use weighted aggregation windows and minimum request thresholds before gating actions take effect.
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix published in Console and Confluence: includes p50/p95/p99 per region and tier
Automated gating rules defined: numeric thresholds for canary, ramp, freeze, rollback stages
Fallback hierarchy documented: preferred fallbacks and exact trigger conditions (latency, error budget, token cost delta)
Rollout engine can evaluate regional metrics and pause/rollback when gate conditions are met
Dashboards show region-by-region SLO attainment and active error budget burn rates
E2E test harness that simulates increased latency in a region and validates fallback execution exists and passes
notes: Design decision: use 10-minute sliding windows with a minimum of 500 requests for region gating to avoid reactive toggles in low-traffic zones
Trade-off: stricter p95 for Premium slows rollouts but reduces customer complaints; recommend asymmetric thresholds by tier
We will expose an 'SLO override' annotation in Console for enterprise customers requiring custom SLOs (implementation as follow-up)
implementation_notes: Engineering will need metric hooks for per-region p50/p95/p99 and per-route token-cost deltas
Routing: add priority to fallback variants in model catalog metadata (e.g., variant: quant8-small, cache-enabled-medium)
Console: new rollout gate UI rows and API fields for region-scoped gates; tie to existing canary/ramp stages
